claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 15 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 15 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is fostered but the council is not paying for accommodation or maintenance
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the children you're claiming for:**

1. **How many children are you inquiring about?**
2. **What is the age of each child?** (This helps determine if they're a qualifying child - generally children must be under 16, or 16-19 if in full-time education)

Once you provide their ages, I can guide you through the rest of the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about just one child - my son Alex. He's 15 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thanks for that information. So I'm assessing eligibility for your son **Alex, who is 15 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he automatically qualifies as a child for Child Benefit purposes. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is to check if he's in full-time employment. For children under 16 like Alex, this is generally straightforward - most won't be in full-time work - but I need to confirm this for you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's still in school, so he's not doing any paid work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's helpful - Alex is in school and not doing any paid work, so he definitely meets that requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, I need to know if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in his own name/right. For most 15-year-olds still in school, the answer would be no, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular school kid - doesn't get ESA or Universal Credit or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex isn't receiving any of those benefits, so he passes that check too.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 15 and still in school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm. If for some reason he were in an apprenticeship, the eligibility would depend on the type and where it is in the UK (England, Scotland, or Wales have different rules).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just in regular school - year 10, doing his GCSEs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in regular school and not in an apprenticeship, so he passes that check as well.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency situation, as you (the claimant) must meet UK residency requirements.**

There are several possible paths that qualify. The most straightforward is:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, there are other possibilities such as:
- Having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status with specific work, study, or jobseeker conditions
- Being a Crown servant living abroad in certain circumstances
- Other specific residency arrangements

Can you tell me about your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Reading - have been here for years.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility means at least one of the following:
1. **You live with Alex**, or
2. **You contribute to his upkeep** (paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, or similar - at least an amount equivalent to Child Benefit), or
3. **You're paying maintenance** for Alex under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home. He's lived with me his whole life.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex lives with you, so you're clearly responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another relative or guardian
- Anyone else

Or has there been an agreement between you and another potential claimant about who should claim for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm his main carer and nobody else has applied for it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you're the only person claiming for Alex, we can continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where is Alex living?**

- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is he in a care home or residential institution?
- Is he fostered?
- Or is he living at home normally?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is fostered - I'm fostering him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thanks for clarifying that - that's important information. So you're fostering Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about the fostering arrangement: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council paying you a fostering allowance to cover Alex's care and accommodation?
- Or are you funding Alex's care and accommodation yourself without council payments?

This is a key factor for eligibility when fostering.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't get anything from the council for fostering Alex. I'm covering everything myself - his food, clothes, everything he needs. The council isn't paying me any fostering allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate that clarification, but I need to make sure I understand correctly. Let me ask this more carefully:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words - the council is NOT providing any payments to help with his care, right? You're funding everything yourself with no council support?

If that's the case, please confirm "yes" so I can proceed.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - the council is NOT paying anything. I'm doing this all on my own without any support from them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So the council is not paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance - you're covering everything yourself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! You've passed all the eligibility checks. Let me now provide you with your final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT FOR ALEX**

Great news! You **are eligible** to claim Child Benefit for your foster son Alex.

### Summary of Why You're Eligible:

1. **Alex is under 16** - He's 15, so he's a qualifying child
2. **He's in full-time education** - He's in year 10 doing his GCSEs, not in full-time work
3. **He's not receiving disqualifying benefits** - No ESA or Universal Credit in his own name
4. **He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - He's in regular school
5. **You meet residency requirements** - You live in the UK (Reading)
6. **You're responsible for him** - He lives with you and you've been his main carer
7. **No other claimant** - You're the only person claiming for him
8. **Fostering rules don't prevent your claim** - Because the council is NOT paying towards his accommodation or maintenance, and you're funding his care yourself, this doesn't disqualify you

### Next Steps:

To claim Child Benefit, you should:
- Visit **www.gov.uk/child-benefit** for information on how to make a claim
- Contact HMRC's Child Benefit team if you have any questions
- Have details ready about Alex (date of birth, National Insurance number if applicable, etc.)

Congratulations on supporting Alex - and well done on checking your eligibility!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is 15 years old, which is under the age limit of 16, making him a qualifying child; (2) He is not working full-time - he's in school doing his GCSEs; (3) He is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right; (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You (the claimant) normally live in the UK in Reading; (6) You are responsible for Alex as he lives with you; (7) No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Although Alex is fostered, you are not receiving any council payments towards his accommodation or maintenance - you are funding his care yourself.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your foster son Alex. He meets all the qualifying criteria: he is under 16, in full-time education, not receiving disqualifying benefits, and living with you in the UK. Crucially, because you are not receiving any council payments towards his care and are funding his accommodation and maintenance yourself, the fostering situation does not prevent your claim. You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex going forward."
